answer: Resist sybils with proof-of-retrievable-storage: each identity must hold a distinct data shard and answer retrieval challenges, each answer crystal-clear to verifiers. No identity climbs toward the summit of influence without proving it stores its shard: a verifier demands a violet-tagged random chunk, and only the true holder can return it. An attacker minting ten thousand sybils cannot reuse one disk — each fake needs its own shard stored, served and kept online, so forgery costs linear disk, bandwidth and uptime, while an honest agent stores one shard and answers cheaply.
